components.heading: Classification
components.text: 2.1 Classification

components.heading: The members of the Association shall be
Land surveyor members shall be persons who:
components.text:
2.1.2 Land surveyor members shall be persons who:
(a) Are entitled to vote;
(b) Are entitled to hold office; and
(c) Have the right to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

components.heading: Life members shall be persons who have been
components.text:
2.1.3 Life members shall be persons who have been
land surveyor members for a total of at least twenty years
and have made substantial contributions to the
Association and/or the land surveying profession and
who :
(a) Are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(b) Are not entitled to vote unless holding office
and have met all MCE requirements;
(c) Are entitled to hold office; and
(d) Are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

components.heading: Honorary members shall be persons who,
components.text:
2.1.4 Honorary members shall be persons who,
through their close association with land surveying for a
period of over ten years, have contributed greatly to the
advancement of the profession and the Association and
who:
(a) Are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(b) Are not entitled to vote;
(c) Are not entitled to hold office; and
(d) Are not entitled to practice land surveying .
Added January 2019

components.heading: Surveyor - in - training members shall be persons
components.text:
2.1.5 Surveyor - in - training members shall be persons
who are candidates seeking admission or readmission as
a member of the Association and who:
(a) Are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(b) Are not entitled to vote;
(c) Are not entitled to hold office; and
(d) Are not entitled to practice land surveying
Added January 2019

components.heading: Associate members shall be persons who :
components.text:
2.1.6 Associate members shall be persons who :
(a) Have the following qualifications:
i . They are now or were qualified to practice land
surveying in any jurisdiction other than New
Brunswick.
ii. They have been engaged in work which is closely
allied to land surveying for a period of at least five
years; or
iii. They have been engaged in the teaching of
surveying for a period of at least five years; and
(b) Have the following rights, privileges and duties:
i. They are entitled to any and all notices from the
association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled.
ii. They are not entitled to vote;
iii. Are not entitled to hold office; and
iv. They are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

components.heading: Retired members shall be persons who :
components.text:
2.1.7 Retired members shall be persons who :
(a) have been previously a land surveyor member; and
(b) they are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(c) they are not entitled to vote unless holding office
and have met all MCE requirements ;
(d) they are entitled to hold office; and
(e) they are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 2019

components.heading: Student members shall be persons who are
components.text:
2.1.8 Student members shall be persons who are
enrolled as a full time, part - time or correspondent
student in a geomatics program or a related academic
program and who:
(a) are entitled to any and all notices from the
Association to which a land surveyor member would be
entitled;
(b) are not entitled to vote;
(c) are not entitled to hold office; and
(d) are not entitled to practice land surveying.
Added January 201 9

components.heading: Registration as a land surveyor member must be
components.text:
2. 3 .1 Registration as a land surveyor member must be
approved by the Council . Revised January 2019

components.heading: Registration as a life member or an honorary
components.text:
2.3.2 Registration as a life member or an honorary
member shall occur as follows:
(a) Nomination shall be made to the Council in a
form prescribed by Council by two members,
both of whom must be land surveyor members.
(b) The nominee must agree to the nomination.
(c) The membership must be approved by a two -
thirds majority of the Council.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: Registration as an associate member or retired
components.text:
2.3.3 Registration as an associate member or retired
member must be approved by a two - thirds majority of
the Council. Revised January 2019

components.heading: Registration as a surveyor - in - training shall occur as
components.text:
2.3.4 Registration as a surveyor - in - training shall occur as
follows:
(a) An application for registration by a candidate
must be approved by the majority of the Board.
(b) Approval of the application by the Board will
be issued based on the applicant having one of
the following criteria:
i. possessing a certificate of completion
issued by the CBEPS;
ii. being successfully admitted as a CBEPS
Candidate;
iii. being enrolled in a program in surveying
at an academic level to the satisfaction of
the Board; or
iv. successfully having completed a diploma
or degree program in land surveying at an
academic level satisfactory to the Board.
Revised January 2019

components.heading: An Executive Council vacancy shall be
components.text:
5.3.1 An Executive Council vacancy shall be
created when a member of the Executive Council:
(a) dies;
(b) fails to attend three consecutive meetings of
the Executive Council without the prior consent of
the Executive Council, in which case the person is
deemed to have resigned;
(c) submits a letter of resignation which is
accepted and approved by the Executive Council;
(d) ceases to be a member in good standing of the
Association;
(e) a Councillor from a regional zone changes
residence from one zone to another within the
province, in which case the person is deemed to have
resigned effective at the date of the annual meeting
following the change of residence.

components.text:

components.text:

include:
(a) Acting as Secretary and recording the
minutes for all meetings of the Association and the
Executive Council, and conducting the
correspondence in accordance with the decisions
taken and policies established at such meetings;
(b) acting as Secretary for the administration
committee and such other committees as the
Executive Council may direct;

Examiners;

components.text:

(c) keeping proper records, showing the source
and disposition of all income;

Council; and

assigned by the Executive Council.

components.heading: The duties of the Office of the Registrar shall
components.text:

include:
(a) keeping a Register in which shall be entered
the name, address, the date of registration of the Land
Surveyors, and Partnerships, Associations of
Persons, or Corporations holding a certificate of
authorization;
(b) recording in the Register the names of
members removed, with the date and reason for
removal;

eligible to vote and to hold office, for use at the
annual meeting and for the conduct of elections; and

together with all supporting documents.

components.heading: Professional Misconduct is defined as
components.text:
8.3.1 Professional Misconduct is defined as
follows:
(a) the conduct of a practitioner which, in the
opinion of the Discipline Committee, is detrimental
to the interests of the public and contravenes the
Canons of Ethics of the profession;
(b) the breach by a Land Surveyor of the
standards of surveying established by the
Association; and
(c) negligence, misrepresentation or any other
conduct which, in the opinion of the Discipline
Committee, renders a Land Surveyor unfit to practice
land surveying.

14. CANONS OF ETHICS

components.heading: As the keystone of professional conduct is
components.text:
14.1 .1 As the keystone of professional conduct is
integrity, it is the duty of land surveyors to practice
the profession according to these Canons of Ethics.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will conduct his work to a
components.text:
14. 1. 2 A Land Surveyor will conduct his work to a
high professional standard always maintaining the
dignity and honor of the profession and protecting the
public interest.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will cooperate, on a
components.text:
14. 1.3 A Land Surveyor will cooperate, on a
continuing basis, in extending the effectiveness of the
survey profession by interchanging information and
professional knowledge with his fellow professionals
and student surveyors and by contributing to the work
and objectives of the Association.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will not act as an expert
components.text:
14. 1.4 A Land Surveyor will not act as an expert
except in areas where he has personal knowledge and
honest conviction.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will not sanction or sign in
components.text:
14. 1. 5 A Land Surveyor will not sanction or sign in
a professional capacity any work not executed under
his personal supervision and professional knowledge.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will exercise due restraint
components.text:
14. 1. 6 A Land Surveyor will exercise due restraint
in criticizing another surveyor's work or reputation in
public; recognizing there are professional forums for
such criticisms within the Association.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will guard against any
components.text:
14. 1.7 A Land Surveyor will guard against any
conflict - of - interest situations by disclosing any
possible conflicts to his client and/or employer and by
always putting the honor of his profession before
personal gain.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will not compete in an
components.text:
14. 1. 8 A Land Surveyor will not compete in an
unfair manner with another land surveyor or mislead
his employers or clients with misleading information
or unprofessional advertising.

components.heading: A Land Surveyor will not disclose
components.text:
14. 1. 9 A Land Surveyor will not disclose
information concerning the business affairs of clients
and employers without their consent.

Policy to any member who is named in more than
three claims per policy year.

sections.heading: The conduct of business at a meeting of the
sections.text:

Association shall be governed by Robert's Rules of
Order.

sections.heading: The Executive Council shall appoint an

Surveyors shall be a member of Professional
Surveyors Canada . The Executive Council shall

sections.text:

14. CANONS OF ETHICS

sections.heading: As the keystone of professional conduct is
sections.text:
14.1 .1 As the keystone of professional conduct is
integrity, it is the duty of land surveyors to practice
the profession according to these Canons of Ethics.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will conduct his work to a
sections.text:
14. 1. 2 A Land Surveyor will conduct his work to a
high professional standard always maintaining the
dignity and honor of the profession and protecting the
public interest.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will cooperate, on a
sections.text:
14. 1.3 A Land Surveyor will cooperate, on a
continuing basis, in extending the effectiveness of the
survey profession by interchanging information and
professional knowledge with his fellow professionals
and student surveyors and by contributing to the work
and objectives of the Association.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will not act as an expert
sections.text:
14. 1.4 A Land Surveyor will not act as an expert
except in areas where he has personal knowledge and
honest conviction.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will not sanction or sign in
sections.text:
14. 1. 5 A Land Surveyor will not sanction or sign in
a professional capacity any work not executed under
his personal supervision and professional knowledge.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will exercise due restraint
sections.text:
14. 1. 6 A Land Surveyor will exercise due restraint
in criticizing another surveyor's work or reputation in
public; recognizing there are professional forums for
such criticisms within the Association.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will guard against any
sections.text:
14. 1.7 A Land Surveyor will guard against any
conflict - of - interest situations by disclosing any
possible conflicts to his client and/or employer and by
always putting the honor of his profession before
personal gain.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will not compete in an
sections.text:
14. 1. 8 A Land Surveyor will not compete in an
unfair manner with another land surveyor or mislead
his employers or clients with misleading information
or unprofessional advertising.

sections.heading: A Land Surveyor will not disclose
sections.text:
14. 1. 9 A Land Surveyor will not disclose
information concerning the business affairs of clients
and employers without their consent.

sections.heading: A Mandatory Continuing Education Program
sections.text:
18.1 .1 A Mandatory Continuing Education Program
will be established and administered by the
Association, facilitated by a Practice Review
Committee under the direction of the Executive
Council.

sections.heading: All Land Surveyor Members, with the
sections.text:
18. 1. 2 All Land Surveyor Members, with the
exception of life members, are required to participate
in the Mandatory Continuing Education Program.

sections.heading: The purpose of the Mandatory Continuing
sections.text:
18. 1. 3 The purpose of the Mandatory Continuing
Education Program is to assist in maintaining the
high standard of quality of services which members
provide:
• by encouraging members to engage in educational
activities which maintain and enhance
professional practice; and
• by increasing the participation of members in
Association activities.

sections.heading: The Mandatory Continuing Education
sections.text:
18. 1. 4 The Mandatory Continuing Education
Program shall include a credit system to be
established by the Practice Review Committee and
approved by Council.
Revised January 2019

sections.heading: The Practice Review Committee will
sections.text:
18.1.5 The Practice Review Committee will
determine the eligibility of courses and course types,
seminars, workshops, Association activities, etc. and
establish a point rating for each. The point rating
system will be based on the relevancy of the course
or activity to the Association and to the practice of
Land Surveying.

sections.heading: The Practice Review Committee shall
sections.text:
18.1.6 The Practice Review Committee shall
distribute a detailed list of possible course types,
seminars, activities etc. to participating members.
Members required to participate in the program may
recommend other courses, activities etc. to the
Committee. Th ese will be reviewed and, if deemed
acceptable, will be included in the Mandatory
Continuing Education Program.

sections.heading: The Association will maintain a current
sections.text:

record of points accumulated by each member
required to participate in the Mandatory Continuing
Education Program .

sections.heading: Participating members shall report all MCE
sections.text:

points using the “Annual Registration Form” and
submit it to the Association no later than January 31
each year.

and make a recommendation to Council.

19. Survey Plans

sections.heading: Requirement for Preparation of a Survey
sections.text:
19.0 Requirement for Preparation of a Survey
Plan subsequent to boundary monumentation
Any Survey Plan of a property will be prepared
according to Section G - 4 of the Standards Manual.
All surveys that result in monuments being placed
shall have a Survey Plan prepared according to
Section G - 4 of the Standards Manual.
The exception to this is when the placed
monumentation is in compliance with existing
coordinated plans that are:
a) referenced to the ANBLS Plan Validation
Database, or
b) registered in the Registry Office or Land
Titles Office for the Province of New
Brunswick.
Added January 2020
